dshBase.status: session-host + worker-http + official session rpc bridge

reuse.reason: Official session-controller Host is Node-only; this is the Workers-native fork of its Session Remote contract. RRULE syntax, timezone/DST, COUNT bounds and occurrence resolution directly reuse the platform-neutral RRule export from the pinned dsh-util-time public entrypoint. DirectoryPicker preserves the official Remote/types and unchanged official browse UI; Node filesystem backends cannot mount in Workers, so the Host seam exposes durable owner-scoped logical directories instead. Exact event-prefix forks directly reuse the stable dsh-session/fork buildForkSeed export. Cron and DST gaps/overlaps directly use the pinned stable dsh-util-time exports. Committed SQL notifications and atomic per-session projection revisions adapt the Host data plane without browser wall-clock sequence fabrication. The remoteAccess/follow seam preserves the official owner baseline contract only after resolving the authenticated user's actual Host; it never accepts client-supplied owners or grants. Official ApprovalService/SystemPrompt notices and current policy context are persisted atomically with policy facts and exposed through a non-waking next-step Host port. Completed tool-history repair uses only existing Agent SDK evidence, without executing a model or tool.
gaps: Session create cwd can address only registered logical Workspaces. Ungrouped Sessions at arbitrary unregistered directories are unavailable and rejected explicitly; the official Workspace-based composer remains supported.
Session events and history are projected from Think admitted history and the Host queue; this is a compatibility contract, not official engine equivalence.
toolResults/watch replays retained durable tool results after reload; the official service is live-only.
DirectoryPicker browses durable logical workspace directories, not a native operating-system filesystem; native pick is explicitly unavailable.

Ordinary uploaded files use durable R2-backed receipts and an 8 MiB deployment limit. Server image normalization is unavailable: official image limits disable new image admission, and image upload/read returns an explicit unavailable error.

Historical imported/forked messages without a provable submission lifecycle retain unknown outcomes; truncated forks use the official forked outcome. Legacy random user ids are correlated only for a unique one-to-one prompt match; ambiguous legacy approvals remain unavailable. Live turns use durable request identities and authoritative Think completion across tool approvals.
Session permissions enforce the real logical R2 file boundary through the marked official permission fork. They do not provide native process sandboxing or network confinement.

Exact chat-event forks persist the official seed and conservative closers and exclude future tool results. Permission facts currently inherit the source effective policy rather than reconstructing its historical chat cursor; missing cut-specific cumulative usage is not invented.

Projection values use an atomic durable per-session revision independent of the dense chat cursor. This supports reliable cross-tab updates but is not the official single native event-derived watermark.
New model/effort choices are durable and frozen at input admission. Old pending executions without their original configuration fail closed rather than using the current picker.

Official native terminal, dynamic Cordis execution, production HMR and full subagent lifecycle remain unavailable; dynamic loading and subagent support are unfinished integrations, not blanket Workers impossibilities.
RemoteAccess is owner-only. The authenticated mux identity selects the owner Host; shared non-owner Peer policy/grant management is not implemented or advertised.

Permission commands and model-facing policy notices are not yet unified into the canonical UI event journal; full native Agent inbox scheduling/cancellation, Auto review and per-operation escalation remain unimplemented. No notification is counted as an admitted user Turn.
